newsitem.title: USA: Arco says debt buyback resulted in Q2 charge.
newsitem.headline: Arco says debt buyback resulted in Q2 charge.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO) repurchased outstanding bonds with a total face value of $756 million during the 1997 second quarter and will take an extraordinary after-tax charge of $118 million, the company announced Thursday.

Net income in future quarters is expected to benefit from lower net interest expense, the company said. Funds for the repurchases came from ARCO's cash balances and commercial paper, the company said.
Terry Dallas, ARCO senior vice president and treasurer, said the repurchases were made as part of ARCO's ongoing liability and debt portfolio management.
Separately, Dallas said that on July 2 ARCO called for redemption of its 10.25 percent Eurobonds which had a face value of $250 million and were due in 2000.
The bonds were called at a price of 101.5 percent of par value. This redemption is expected to result in an after-tax charge of $2 million in the 1997 third quarter, ARCO said.

In March, ARCO announced its intention to settle its nine percent exchangeable notes due September 15, 1997, with Lyondell Petrochemical Company stock owned by ARCO. That action removed $988 million in debt from the company's balance sheet, ARCO said.
